prerequisites: It is recommended that the student has taken the courses "Computadores" (Computers) and "Infraestructura informática y de Red" (IT and Network Infrastructure).
Practical knowledge of programming languages explained in "Metodología de la Programación" (Programming Methodology).
Ability to read and understand documentation written in English.

learning_outcomes.text: Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their area of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (normally within their area of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Students can transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.

Choose and apply the most appropriate methods and techniques to analyze and solve problems defined by data that represent a challenge due to their volume, velocity, variety or heterogeneity, including computational, mathematical, statistical and signal processing methods.

Have the experimental and analytical skills to work autonomously, being able to propose experiments and describe, analyze, evaluate and interpret the resulting information to propose alternative and novel solutions to known and/or emerging problems.
Create models and make decisions based on available data, combining acquired knowledge and being able to apply new knowledge for problem solving.
Ability to integrate into a multidisciplinary team within the framework of a data science project.
Ability to express data processing results clearly and convincingly, both in writing and orally.
Understand computer architecture and identify and evaluate the performance and scalability of computer systems used for processing large volumes of data.
Know and understand the concept of a distributed system.
Understand communication between services and their aggregation.
Understand the different architectural models of distributed systems and select the most appropriate for a given problem.
Design and deploy distributed systems using cloud services.
Know and apply techniques to increase reliability, availability, and performance in distributed systems.

syllabus_topics: Communication between services at the socket level
Consumption and development of APIs over HTTP
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as 0.45 * TEO + 0.4 * PRAC + 0.05 * ASIST + 0.1 * CV, provided all minimums are met. A minimum of 4.5/10 is required in the average of theoretical controls (TEO) and in the average of practical block (PRAC). A minimum of 4.5/10 (70% attendance) is required for practical assistance (ASIST). If any minimum is not reached, the qualification is the minimum between the calculated score and 4.0. For the extraordinary call, students who did not pass the continuous assessment can take a theoretical exam (ET) and a practical exam (EP). A minimum of 4.5 is required in both ET and EP. If both minimums are reached, the final grade is 0.50 * ET + 0.50 * EP; otherwise, the grade will be the minimum between the formula and 4.0. For differentiated evaluation, the final grade is 50% theoretical exam and 50% practical exam.
